data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in Jordan performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results changed relative to earlier PISA cycles (notably mathematics from 2012 to 2022). Jordan participated for the first time in PISA in 2022, and the assessment used two two-hour tests with different students receiving different subject combinations; items included multiple-choice and constructed-response tasks. The document reports mean performance trends, proficiency-level attainment (e.g., Level 2 and Level 5/6 shares), and within-country gaps by socio-economic status and gender, alongside contextual indicators such as belonging, discipline in mathematics lessons, safety, parental involvement, and COVID-related learning experiences. Because this is a descriptive reporting factsheet that cites OECD’s PISA 2022 Database tables, it does not present an original ML modeling pipeline, PV combination method, or missing-data procedure in the text provided.
